notes.title: HUGE PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENTS in next update
notes.notes:
Hi to all,

[h2]PREAMBLE[/h2]
When AMD published their new OpenGL drivers in 2021 the performance imrpovement of S2engine on Radeon cards was really impressive. 
AMD OpenGL drivers now are much much much more performant that NVIDIA ones (even if NVIDIA stability remained unsurpassed), that still keep a big overhead.
From my point of view this is a shame: NVIDIA cards are the most performant and widespread cards on the market and I really don't want S2engine to underperform on those cards.
So,
In the last month I've worked on a new rendering system to reduce the gap between AMD and NVIDIA driver performances.

[h2]AZDO[/h2]
Today I'm proud to announce that I've just closed the hard part of the development of a new rendering system based on some AZDO (Approaching Zero Driver Overhead) functions that will improve about 30%-45% the performances on NVIDIA cards by reducing the driver overhead!

Results of the tests I've done on some s2engine demos are really impressive.

Following are OLD / NEW comparison screenshots of the Building Generator DLC city level, 
The reference system specs are:
CPU - INTEL i5 8600K
GPU - NVIDIA GTX 1060 6GB
RAM - 16GB

Here, instead, are come comparison screenshots related to the UPCOMING New Cementery Pack, on the same reference system:

Finally are some comparison screenshots in HELLSEED (on the same reference system):
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/23073876/4ec4eaa2bad3885a046e77a0147c1f1989968c81.jpg[/img]

As you can see from these screenshots the improvements are HUGE.
The AZDO way seems to be the right way for an incredible performance evolution of the engine, so I'll continue to develop it by including all the remaining most recent AZDO functions in future.

[h2]ABOUT RADEONS[/h2]
As said AMD OpenGL drivers are today very very performant (in some cases they are still faster than NVIDIA ones) and they seems to work fine with and without AZDO, so the new rendering system seems to produce no improvement.
This conclusion could be not completely true due to the fact that my AMD reference system is very limited in graphics card (I use an old and poor RX550), so with a more performant and modern system results could change.
[b]SO LET ME KNOW if you notice improvement on your RADEON card when the new update will be public.[/b]

For now it's all,
Stay Tuned,
PROFENIX STUDIO

notes.title: EasyGamePack update coming soon
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/23073876/7291dda31cfc2223e307d62baa6c5a1109f89232.png[/img]

Hi guys,

In these last weeks, waiting for finishing the multi-threading system re-design and finally starting the implementation of the new S2ENGINE HD 2019.2 version, I've found time for implementing new features for EasyGamePack DLC.

First I've extended the possibilities provided by the inventory system.
Now it is possible to collect documents and examining objects, in addition to using them.
Also it is possible to customize inventory layout using tabs and grids for managing items and weapons.
Also I've integrated an ad-hoc key-target management to guarantee that a key is used only in proximity of its target (or pointing at its target in case of first person).

I've also integrated a smart commands visualization that changes itself if you are using kayboard+mouse or a Pad, commands can be visualized on screen on demand (using GameMachine), the system will be responsible to show the right command icon.

The last feature is the current objective notification (with a fade-in, fade-out animation) and the notification of player actions (ex. picked up a key, used a key, etc..)

For showing all these improvements I've made a test using EasyGamePack with Haunted House DLC simulating an horro game like Resident Evil 7.

Following is the result:
[previewyoutube=k8nHim2Gs_c;full][/previewyoutube]
For now it is all,
Stay tuned!
 
PROFENIX STUDIO

notes.title: UPDATE TO VERSION 2018.1.11
notes.notes:
Hi guys,

Today we have published a new update for 2018.1 version.

Main improvements are following:

[h1]CUBE OBJECTS CACHE[/h1]
We have implemented a "geometry cache" for CubeObjects that makes possible to have hardware instancing of cubeObjects having the same dimensions, improving A LOT the drawing performances.
This makes cubeObjects to be really "usable", in the sense that now they are treated just as all other static objects (meshObjects).

The following is an image BEFORE cubeObject "geometry cache", showing many stacked cubeObjects to form a building structure:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23073876/7b49af4838598dd1c06261abf95ed82f193aecc3.jpg[/img]
If you zoom the image you can see the superimposed profiling text "FPS: 20.0000" on top of the image.

The following image is AFTER cubeObject "geometry cache" implementation:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23073876/13213bb4a07564875a531ec9a29b338c92e3e7fa.jpg[/img]
If you zoom the image you can see the superimposed profiling text "FPS: 60.0000" on top of the image.

A really great performance improvement

[h1]IMPROVED COLLISION TESTS[/h1]
In particular Characters collision tests ([b]CharacterCollisionTest[/b] and [b]CharacterIsOnGround[/b] Game Machine actions).

Usually characters collided with a capsule collision shape, this capsule has a "padding" used for avoiding possible round-off errors.

The drawback is that this "padding" isn't used when performing the "sweep tests" used in [b]CharacterCollisionTest[/b] and [b]CharacterIsOnGround[/b] Game Machine actions. 

This causes sometimes "false positive", in the sense that the Sweep Test fails
while the capsule continues to collide, traducing in [b]CharacterIsOnGround[/b] returning FALSE (the character is still in air) while character is really just colliding with ground.

[b]WHAT IS THE SOLUTION?[/b] 
the solution is to give a "padding" also to the Sweep Test, the same padding you have used for the character capsule.
This is why we have introduced a "skinWidth" parameter into the character class and a "padding" parameter into "CharacterIsOnGround" and "CharacterCollisionTest" actions.

[h1]IMPROVED PHYSICS TRIGGERS[/h1]
Apart from some bugs affecting the 2018.1.10 version, now triggers perfectly report the lists of objects inside and objects exiting from. Reports can be easily catched by GameMachine.

[h1]IMPROVED MOVING PLATFORMS[/h1]
By introducing the aforementioned "skinWidth" parameter to character class, by improving the physics triggers and finally introducing some new action we have also improved the possibility to create moving platform using Game Machine just introduced into 2018.1.10 version.
Now platforms are more stable also at low framerates.

notes.title: S2ENGINE HD 2018.1 PREVIEW BEFORE RELEASE
notes.notes:
Hi to all,

I'm very sorry for the big big big delay.

I know, I haven't published news for months. 
I've worked night & day to the new update, adding a lot of new things and I haven't had sufficient time to stop and think to write a "progress state" announce for a lot of time.

Today I have finally kept a bit of time for talking about What you could expect from the new S2ENGINE HD update.

First
[h1]THE NAME[/h1]
For a long time I've talked about the next update as S2ENGINE HD 1.4.6 B10 version, but, while working on it I realized that the changes are so BIG that it hadn't sense to continue calling it 1.4.6 B10, so I decided to change the version naming.
Starting from the next S2ENGINE I'll call it by keeping the year of releasing and an incremental index of the version, so the name will be S2ENGINE HD 2018.1, 2018.2, 2018.3, etc.. for this year, and 2019.1, 2019.2, etc.. for next year and so on.

[h1]NEW EDITOR INTERFACE[/h1]
The big big big change from the previous versions will be the editor interface. 
I've collected all the community suggestions, giving a look to the "today standards", and took a very "HARD" decision: 

Re-thinking the editor interface!

The changes are too many for a detailed explaination, SO
Take a look to the latest preview/tutorial videoclips I've uploaded on YouTube:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F1hQxBalM2s&t=1481s https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qSBPWpxnceI&t=540s
As their names suggest they are thought not only as PREVIEW of the new version BUT ALSO as FIRST TUTORIALS

[h1]NEW PBR[/h1]
Following suggestions and requests of a part of the engine community I've completely re-designed the Physically Based Rendering system:

The new PBR shaders are based on GGX equations and roughness/metal workflow, that is the "basic workflow" of the majority of industry-standard tools such as, for example, Substance products.

The following is a sequence showing a blue coloured material with metalness=0 and roughness from 0 to 1:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23073876/504cc0481bf8c59b273351862d81853f756cf8e8.jpg[/img]
The following is a sequence showing a yellow coloured material with metalness=1 and roughness from 0 to 1:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23073876/7dfdb8e111a5994a5e9c74d667f9249fd92dbab8.jpg[/img]

[h1]NEW OUTDOOR RENDERING[/h1]
The new PBR system forced me to also re-think the whole outdoor rendering. 

[b]ATMOSPHERIC SCATTERING[/b]
I've investigated for weeks about how it was the best way to render realistic atmospheric scattering without too many parameters to change (as in previous versions). 

Finally I came across the famous "precomputed atmospheric scattering" by Eric Bruneton. 

The results were awesome: 
No more need for a lot of parameters and all colors, sun, sky, fog, from sunrise to sunset, were just like reality.

The drawback of this tech is that the precomputation of LUTs, even if it is powered by GPU, cannot be executed in realtime, so changing some parameters like Mie and Rayleigh scattering or wavelength colors (for simulating various weather conditions) is too much slow. 

So I've also implemented a "distributed interpolated over frames precomputation of LUTs". In this way changing weather conditions is possible at the cost of changing them not too much fast, just as in reality :D

[b]CLOUDS[/b]
AT THIS POINT, made a SO REALISTIC SKY forced me to also change clouds rendering.
Clouds are very very very complex matter :)

I based my work on different papers, in particular on "Horizon Zero Dawn" and  "Frostbite engine" clouds systems.
Clouds are rendered into a 3D layer raymarching the scattering from sky and sun. 

Putting it all together was an astonishing show as you can see from the following image:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23073876/eb1955713e83bb3b18e7489f0e68389aa3714bb4.jpg[/img]

Of course clouds are computed in realtime and a lot of parameters, like density, amount of water, scattering, and so on..., can be changed during the day.

THE ONLY LIMITATION FOR NOW is that you cannot fly trough clouds, they are only rendered as background.

The transition from day to night is absolutely smooth and you can see the moon reflecting on the environment and clouds around it when the sun is still colouring the environment and the clouds by its side!!

[b]OCEAN[/b]
Finally I've also improved the ocean, either rendering (improved sss and better foam) and simulation.
In this version the ocean supports beaufort scale.
This means you can set parameters for every ocean state (amount of foam, micro and macro waves height and normals, and so on...), from calm to rough, and then, with a single slider, change the ocean state during the time of day.

The following image gives an idea of what I mean:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23073876/742891b797bace868124a700f702c721f52d997e.jpg[/img]

[h1]OTHER IMPROVEMENTS[/h1]
As announced in previous posts I have:
[list]
[*] improved and bugfixed some other subsystems like:
[list]
 [*]Model importing
 [*]Texture managing (new STX format) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E6kew06Fagk&t=18s
[/list]
[*] I've implemented a Load/Save game system https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ha5-Ne2c0fc https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TZEUeODHnhU
[*] I've introduced Layers
[*] Last But Not Least I've Added Exporting and Texture Atlas Editing into the BUILDING GENERATOR PLUGIN https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aa7xRKUH34M&t=910s
[/list]

[h1]CONCLUSION[/h1]
In conclusion this update will contain very exciting new features BUT MOST IMPORTANT It will be the FIRST STEP for a BETTER user experience!

The next step before releasing is THE SECOND TEST PHASE and the update of all DLCs and Packages. 
Due to BIG changes, it should be another "night&day" hard work...I hope not too much long in time ;)

Cross fingers :D

The release is close... 
stay tuned guys :)
